key_insight: A learned patient world model could support multiple ICU policy simulations without rebuilding question-specific patient-state models.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help health systems explore how ICU capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfers affect care demand, queues, and bed use before implementation.
method: Train a neural network on longitudinal MIMIC-IV electronic health records to represent patient trajectories.
Freeze the model and connect time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues.
Reconfigure scenario-specific mappings to simulate different operational policies.
evidence_signal: In MIMIC-IV-based simulations, the model matched Markov and semi-Markov comparators on aggregate occupancy and directional policy responses, while capturing a history-dependent 24-hour recovery difference of −6.4 percentage points versus −6.7 observed.
watch_item: Simulation results do not establish real-world operational benefit; external validation and prospective evaluation are needed before deployment.
paper_title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
